subject.title: Slack: support assistant.threads.setSuggestedPrompts for dynamic prompt suggestions

question: Should OpenClaw add a public Slack-native suggested-prompts config/action surface, or should contextual prompt suggestions be owned by Smart Replies/ClawHub plugins using the existing presentation hook path?
rationale: The Slack API primitive and shipped default prompts already exist, but the remaining request changes public config and agent-facing message-action contracts; the exact implementation PR was closed in favor of plugin ownership without a final decision on this issue.

options.title: Delegate To Plugin Path
options.body: Confirm that contextual suggestions belong in Smart Replies or another ClawHub plugin, and narrow or close this issue to any missing host API if one remains.

options.title: Approve Slack-Native Contract
options.body: Add a supported Slack plugin config and dynamic action for native `assistant.threads.setSuggestedPrompts`, with schema, docs, compatibility review, and focused tests.

options.title: Keep Fixed Defaults Only
options.body: Treat the shipped manifest/runtime default prompts as the supported Slack assistant prompt behavior and close the configurable/dynamic request as not planned.

recommendation.title: Delegate To Plugin Path
recommendation.body: Confirm that contextual suggestions belong in Smart Replies or another ClawHub plugin, and narrow or close this issue to any missing host API if one remains.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged Slack assistant lifecycle work and is the strongest current-history owner for deciding whether this stays in the Slack plugin or moves to a plugin/ClawHub path.
